original_target.title: Can nonparallel cylinder packings approach optimal lower density?

full_original_statement:
Let $`\mathfrak C`$ be the class of countably infinite families $`\mathcal C=\{C_i\}`$ of solid infinite circular cylinders of radius 1 in $`\mathbb R^3`$. Their interiors must be pairwise disjoint, and no two axes may be parallel. Define the lower density by
```math
\delta^-(\mathcal C)=\liminf_{R\to\infty}
 \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(B_R(0)\cap\bigcup_i C_i)}
      {\mathrm{Vol}(B_R(0))}.
```

Is
```math
\sup_{\mathcal C\in\mathfrak C}\delta^-(\mathcal C)
 =\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{12}}?
```

Equivalently, can the lower density exceed $`\pi/\sqrt{12}-\varepsilon`$ for every $`\varepsilon>0`$? Attainment by one packing is not required.

sources.scope_comparison: The actual construction reaches pi/sqrt12 for upper density (limsup), while its lower-density construction gives pi/6−epsilon. The paper explicitly distinguishes limsup, liminf, and densities with variable centers. The target requires liminf about one fixed center arbitrarily close to pi/sqrt12, so the upper-density theorem and bounded-hole questions do not resolve it. No later full matching claim found.
